findings.issue_text: Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb crashes with NoMethodError on db:migrate for fresh installs and any site that never set embed_category (or has it set to the default empty string ''): the INNER JOIN on site_settings.value = categories.name returns zero rows, execute(...)[0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises before the intended category_id == 0 fallback to uncategorized can ever run, making the fallback unreachable and blocking the entire upgrade (fix: execute(...)[0].try(:[], 'id').to_i, or run the fallback query first).

Migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim into the new table, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization; the old allows_embeddable_host? stripped http(s)://, so protocol-prefixed entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' were previously supported, but they can never match the new where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) lookup, causing previously-allowed embed sites to silently receive 403 Discourse::InvalidAccess ('invalid referer host') after upgrade with no error surfaced anywhere.
The migration's raw SQL INSERT interpolates legacy host values unescaped (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)), so an apostrophe in a legacy host value breaks the INSERT and crashes the migration.
Blank lines in the legacy embeddable_hosts setting are copied into the new table as empty-string hosts, rendering as junk rows in the admin embeddable hosts table.

EmbeddableHost's format regex explicitly allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}) and before_validation only strips scheme and path, so an admin can save hosts like localhost:3000 or example.com:8080, but record_for_host compares only uri.host (which never includes a port), so port-bearing records silently never authorize any request — either strip ports on save or match against host+port.

There is no referential integrity between embeddable_hosts.category_id and categories (no model validation, no DB foreign key, and category deletion does not clean up hosts): orphaned hosts cause TopicEmbed.import to pass a dead category_id to PostCreator (category: eh.try(:category_id)), breaking subsequent embeds/feed polls, and in the admin UI host.category hydrates to nothing so the edit dialog shows an empty category chooser and saving silently reassigns the host to uncategorized without warning.

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController dereferences EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, so update crashes at host.host = ... and destroy crashes at nil.destroy on stale/missing records; likewise params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises when the param is missing/nil (and a nil host would crash the model's before_validation nil.sub!), producing 500 errors instead of 404/422 responses.

The admin embeddable-host component's host.destroyRecord().then(...) call has no .catch, so failed DELETE requests (500/network) close the bootbox and leave the row in the table with zero indication anything went wrong (plus an unhandled promise rejection), in contrast to save() which correctly calls popupAjaxError.
The new plural branch in _hydrateEmbedded (store.js.es6) calls obj[k].map unconditionally, throwing a TypeError if a payload ever carries *_ids: null.

The plural branch in _hydrateEmbedded unconditionally deletes the original *_ids key and assigns obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [], so when the ids have no side-loaded collection every _lookupSubType returns undefined and the original data is replaced with [undefined, ...] — the || [] guard cannot rescue a non-empty array of undefined — silently dropping bare *_ids attributes on every store hydration, unlike the singular branch which preserves the key when hydration fails.

The fabricator files have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb was git-mv'd to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb while keeping the category definitions, and the new Fabricator(:embeddable_host) was written into category_fabricator.rb, so each file defines the opposite of what its name claims and future edits to category/embeddable-host fabricators will land in the wrong file.

Public embed hot path (embed_controller.rb `ensure_embeddable` → embeddable_host.rb `host_allowed?`/`record_for_host`) now runs an uncached DB query (`where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`) on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request, replacing the previous cached in-memory site-setting allowlist check and adding an uncacheable SQL roundtrip per request on the highest-traffic unauthenticated endpoint; fix by caching the host list in memory/Redis (invalidated on host CRUD) or at minimum loading all rows once per request and comparing in memory.

The hot-path host lookup query is unindexable as written: the migration creates no index on `host`, and the query `lower(host) = ?` cannot use a plain index anyway (would need a functional index on `lower(host)`), guaranteeing a sequential scan on every embed request; fix by normalizing the stored host to lowercase in `before_validation`, adding `add_index :embeddable_hosts, :host`, and querying `where(host: uri.host)`.

Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts crashes on most existing installs: `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError because Discourse only persists site settings changed from defaults, so most installs have no `embed_category` row (and a persisted empty value fails the join too); the fallback at line 15 has the same problem on fresh installs since no `uncategorized_category_id` row exists until seeds run, making `db:migrate` a deploy/upgrade blocker for the majority of forums.

The migration is destructive and irreversible: `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` runs inside `change` with no backup, so rolling back the migration permanently loses the original embedding config (the hosts table is dropped while the source settings are already gone).
SQL injection/breakage in migration line 25: `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` uses string interpolation of the stored host, so a host value containing a quote breaks the SQL or allows injection.

Nil dereference on stale/invalid ids in admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb (lines 10-11, 15-16): `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is passed straight to `save_host`/`.destroy` with no `record_not_found` handling, so a nonexistent id (e.g., double-delete race in the admin UI) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a clean 404.

Fabricator file contents are swapped: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators — functionally harmless (Fabricator globs the directory so everything still registers) but clearly accidental and a maintenance trap.

Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category is unset: site_settings only contains rows for settings changed from YAML defaults, so on fresh installs (where categories is empty until seeding, which runs after db:migrate) the query in 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb returns zero rows, result[0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate for every fresh install and any existing site that never set embed_category; the `if category_id == 0` fallback is dead code since the crash happens before it executes

Migrated host values are inserted unnormalized: the migration copies raw setting values like `https://example.com/1234` verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host, but the new lookup compares lower(host) against the bare referer host (URI(referer).host), so any host configured with scheme/path/port silently starts returning 403 after upgrade; normalization only runs before_validation on save, never for migrated rows

Host validation accepts values the referer check can never match: the regex explicitly permits `example.com:8080` via `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` but record_for_host extracts uri.host (port stripped) and queries lower(host) = 'example.com', so the stored row never matches; the `(\/.*)?` regex branch is dead code since before_validation strips paths first; the API accepts input whose only possible effect is to silently deny embedding

Hard removal of the public embeddable_hosts / embed_category site settings with no deprecation window or caller consideration: the keys vanish from the site_settings.yml schema and the migration irreversibly deletes stored values, so any provisioning script, API client, or plugin using the documented PUT /admin/site_settings/embeddable_hosts endpoint now fails with no release-note migration path to the successor embeddable_hosts resource

No handling for category deletion leaves dangling embeddable_hosts.category_id: the bare belongs_to has no FK constraint and Discourse's category-deletion reassignment flow is unaware of the new table, so deleting a referenced category causes TopicEmbed.import to pass a dead id to PostCreator, topic creation fails, and TopicEmbed.create! raises, breaking embed/feed retrieval for that host until an admin re-saves it; the admin UI also renders a blank category badge

Admin hosts API returns 500 instead of 404/422 for unknown ids and missing params: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first yields nil for nonexistent ids and save_host(nil)/host.destroy then raise NoMethodError; requests missing the embeddable_host param envelope also crash, and a nil host value would crash the model's before_validation sub!

PUT /admin/customize/embedding accepts a body and silently does nothing: the update action never reads params, just re-renders current state and returns 200, and the shipped frontend even calls it (embedding.update({})), making it a contract trap advertising an update capability that doesn't exist

Unquoted string interpolation in the migration INSERT: old setting values are spliced into raw SQL via VALUES ('#{h}', ...), so a value containing a quote aborts/corrupts the migration (an unparameterized SQL vector), and split("\n") can yield blank lines that insert '' hosts which can never match

Dotless hostnames like localhost are no longer savable: the regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` so dotless intranet names are rejected, whereas the old setting compared raw strings and matched them — a capability regression for environments that legitimately embed from localhost/dotless intranet hosts, with only the dev-mode admin bypass remaining

_hydrateEmbedded plural branch destroys raw *_ids keys even when hydration fails: it unconditionally delete obj[k] and replaces it with pluralize(subType) even when _lookupSubType returns undefined for some ids, producing [undefined, ...] since `hydrated || []` never fires on a truthy array, and obj[k].map throws TypeError if a serializer emits *_ids: null; previously plural *_ids keys passed through untouched

Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts crashes with NoMethodError on default data: when no valid 'embed_category' site_settings row exists (fresh installs, sites that never set it, or values matching a renamed/deleted category since the join matches on c.name = s.value), the SELECT returns zero rows and result[0]['id'] raises on nil, aborting db:migrate and blocking deploys; the fallback at lines 14-16 is unreachable because it is gated on category_id == 0 (ids start at 1) and uncategorized_category_id is a computed SiteSetting helper method, not a row in site_settings

Migration copies old embeddable_hosts setting values into the table verbatim without normalization, but the new authorization check (where('lower(host) = ?', uri.host)) only matches a bare lowercase hostname; old values with http(s):// prefixes or paths (explicitly supported by the removed code) never match since before_validation normalization only runs on save, never on the migration's raw INSERTs, so existing embeds silently start failing EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? with 403s and no error surfaced anywhere
The migration's INSERT interpolates the host value h unescaped into SQL, so a stored setting line containing a quote character aborts the migration

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy pass EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first straight into save_host/host.destroy with no nil check, so a stale id (record deleted in another session, double-click/double-delete) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404 or render_json_error, leaving the frontend promise unresolved

EmbeddableHost category_id is never validated and is not cleaned up on category deletion: save_host only coerces blank category_ids to uncategorized while any non-blank numeric value is stored (Rails 4 belongs_to adds no presence validation), and nothing wires EmbeddableHost into Category#destroy, so deleted categories orphan rows and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator with skip_validations: true, causing silent import failures or topics referencing a nonexistent category, with the admin UI showing a blank badge and no error

Malformed requests produce 500s instead of 4xx in the embeddable hosts admin flow: params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises when the embeddable_host key is absent, and a JSON null host makes before_validation's self.host.sub! raise NoMethodError on nil before the format validation can return a friendly 422

Frontend destroyRecord().then(...) in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch (the sibling save correctly uses .catch(popupAjaxError)), so a failed DELETE silently leaves the row in place with no user feedback and an unhandled promise rejection

PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op: the update action ignores the request body entirely and re-renders the same payload as show, while the frontend saveChanges PUTs {} with no error handling — a success-without-persist trap for any future embedding settings added to this singleton

The new plural *_ids hydration branch in store.js.es6 is unguarded and changes key-deletion behavior globally: obj[k].map has no presence check (category_ids: null throws a TypeError that kills hydration for the whole model), it unconditionally deletes the *_ids key even when _lookupSubType hydrates nothing (unlike the singular branch, an un-side-loaded *_ids payload loses its ids and gains an array of undefined), and it writes to naive pluralize(subType) (category_ids -> obj.categorys)

After save, embeddable-host.js.es6 overwrites host.category from the local categoryId instead of the server response: when no category was chosen the server defaults to uncategorized but Discourse.Category.findById(null/undefined) returns nothing, so the badge renders blank and the row disagrees with persisted state until reload

There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on embeddable_host.host and where('lower(host) = ?', host).first has no ORDER BY, so entering the same host twice with different categories makes record_for_host's pick — and therefore which category imported topics land in — arbitrary and nondeterministic between queries

The host format validation regex requires a dotted TLD of 2-5 characters, rejecting dot-less hostnames (localhost, internal names) and longer TLDs that the old free-form setting allowed, breaking intranet/self-hosted embedding setups (dev is only saved by the Rails.env.development? && admin? bypass in embed_controller)

Data migration create_embeddable_hosts (20150818190757) crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row doesn't exist — the default state for most installs since Discourse persists only overridden settings — aborting db:migrate on upgrade; it crashes the same way when the stored value doesn't match a category name, and the 'if category_id == 0' fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code

Migration inserts legacy host values via raw SQL INSERT without the model's before_validation normalization (protocol/path stripping), so entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim and never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's exact 'lower(host) = ?' lookup, silently breaking embedding from previously-allowed hosts after upgrade while the Fabricate-based specs pass
Unescaped string interpolation of host values into the migration's SQL INSERT — a host containing a quote kills the migration

Both new admin controllers (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController) have placeholder-only specs asserting superclass inheritance; no request specs cover create/update/destroy happy paths, the render_json_error branch on invalid hosts, the blank-category_id defaulting to uncategorized, or the serialization shape, giving a false impression the controllers are tested

Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy on a nonexistent id and requests with missing params[:embeddable_host] raise uncaught NoMethodError and return 500 instead of 404, and no spec exercises these unknown-id or malformed-param paths

Zero frontend tests for the entire new admin embedding UI, including the pathFor override, the ADMIN_MODELS basePath change shared by all admin models, addHost/deleteHost, the buffered save/cancel/delete flows, the post-save client-side category patch, and the store hydration the page depends on (plural *_ids hydration tested only via the single-word 'color' fixture, not the real multi-word 'embeddable_host_ids' consumer)

Stale vacuous topic_spec test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' survives the behavioral change where expandable_first_post? no longer consults embeddable hosts; it passes only for unrelated reasons (embed_truncate defaults false, has_topic_embed? false on unstubbed Fabricate.build), and the actual change (embed + truncate + zero hosts now returns true) has no test documenting it

Weakened embed_controller_spec 'missing host' test passes for the wrong reason: it fabricates no host but also doesn't stub a referer, so it fails via the nil-referer path instead of the no-hosts path and can't distinguish the two conditions

Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that accepts nothing and changes nothing (just re-serializes), and embedding.hbs renders no control that sends the frontend saveChanges action, making the PUT dead code — saving embedding settings silently does nothing and nothing in the suite would reveal it

Behavioral change in TopicEmbed.import fallback category is untested: category assignment changed from the global SiteSetting.embed_category to eh.try(:category_id) derived from the URL's host, so when the host isn't a registered EmbeddableHost (e.g., RSS feed polling) topics now silently post to Uncategorized instead of the previously configured category; the spec only covers the matched-host path

New plural hydration branch in store.js (lines 192-197) lacks the singular branch's guardrails: obj[k].map has no null/undefined guard (a null *_ids in any payload throws), failed lookups aren't filtered, and 'hydrated || []' is dead code since arrays are always truthy — failed lookups produce [undefined] records; only the happy path is tested

Fabricator file contents appear accidentally swapped: the :embeddable_host fabricator is defined in category_fabricator.rb and all four category fabricators are in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — functionally harmless but a botched rename that will misdirect anyone maintaining these fixtures

Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb raises NoMethodError on default and fresh installs: when the embed_category setting is unset (its default is an empty string and no category can be named empty), the INNER JOIN matches nothing so [0] is nil and [0]['id'].to_i raises; the `if category_id == 0` fallback never executes and contains the same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern for uncategorized_category_id, so db:migrate aborts for every site that never set embed_category and for all fresh installs

The migration's raw-SQL INSERT stores host values unnormalized, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation protocol/path stripping, while record_for_host matches via lower(host) = uri.host: previously tolerated 'http://'-prefixed entries become rows like 'http://discourse.org' that can never match, so previously working embeds are silently rejected after upgrade, and the DB is left holding rows the model's own format validation would reject

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators; tests pass only because fabricator definitions register globally regardless of file, but the file layout lies about where things live, future edits will land in the wrong file, and git blame is scrambled (likely a botched git mv)
In store.js.es6, the new plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map without guarding against null/undefined *_ids values, so it throws

In store.js.es6, the plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded does not filter failed lookups (unlike the singular branch), so missing sideposts produce false entries that downstream {{#each}} consumers will treat as records

In store.js.es6, the plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded runs `delete obj[k]` unconditionally rather than only on successful hydration (as the singular branch does), destroying the raw ids even when hydration failed
In store.js.es6, `hydrated || []` in the plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded is dead code because map always returns an array, so the intended empty-on-failure guard does nothing

EmbeddableHost's host validation regex is stricter than reality: [a-z]{2,5} caps TLD length at 5, rejecting valid TLDs like .museum and .travel, and the pattern mandates a dot, so dot-less hosts like localhost:3000 can never be whitelisted even though nothing downstream assumes a dotted host
The (\/.*)? alternative in EmbeddableHost's host validation regex is dead code because before_validation strips paths before validation runs

admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy dereference EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check, so a stale or invalid id raises NoMethodError (nil.host= / host.destroy) and returns a 500 instead of a 404

EmbeddableHost's before_validation crashes on a nil host: self.host.sub! assumes a string, so a create/update without host in params (which the controller passes through unchecked) raises NoMethodError instead of producing a 422 validation error

The embedding update path is a dead no-op pipeline: embedding_controller's update ignores the request body and re-renders exactly what show renders, the frontend saveChanges action is never referenced by any template, and the admin.embedding.edit locale key is unused — any client that PUTs changes gets a 200 with its input silently discarded

embeddable-host.js.es6 patches model state from its own local copy instead of the server response: after host.save it sets the category via Discourse.Category.findById in the view layer, re-implementing the store's _hydrateEmbedded hydration, and it diverges from the server, which defaults a blank category to uncategorized — so saving a host with no category chosen leaves the UI rendering no badge while the record actually points at uncategorized
The migration INSERT interpolates raw stored text into SQL ('#{h}'), so a value containing a quote breaks the migration
The migration uses create_table with force: true, which silently drops a pre-existing embeddable_hosts table along with its data
The migration's data operations (INSERTs and DELETE FROM site_settings) sit inside def change, so rollback raises instead of restoring the deleted settings rows

There is no uniqueness constraint on the host column: nothing prevents two identical host rows (format-only validation and no UI check), and record_for_host resolves via unordered .first, so with duplicates carrying different categories the embed destination category is effectively arbitrary; a unique index plus uniqueness validation would make .first deterministic

admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb and admin/embedding_controller.rb re-declare before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff despite inheriting Admin::AdminController, which already enforces staff access; the duplicated auth filters invite drift if base-class policy changes and add no protection

Migration crashes on default installs (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11): the raw SQL assumes the 'embed_category' site setting row exists, but Discourse only persists settings changed from their default, so on most installs the result set is empty and [0] is nil, aborting db:migrate; the INNER JOIN on category name also crashes when the category was renamed, deleted, or the value was stored as an id, and the 'if category_id == 0' fallback is dead code because the code crashes before reaching it (CI misses this since the test DB is built from schema.rb, not by replaying migrations)

Migration irreversibly destroys the source settings (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31): 'DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN (...)' uses raw SQL inside change with no down and no copy of the original values, so db:rollback leaves the settings permanently deleted with no recovery path; use explicit up/down that restores the rows or don't delete until the backfill is verified

Backfill doesn't normalize hosts, so migrated embeds silently break (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22-25): the INSERT copies raw setting values verbatim, but lookups (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) require an exact bare hostname; the old implementation tolerated protocol-prefixed entries, so a row stored as 'http://eviltrout.com' can never match a referer host after migration, and blank lines in the setting become empty-string junk rows; the specs don't catch this because Fabricate goes through the model's before_validation normalization which the migration bypasses

Unescaped SQL interpolation in the migration backfill (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25): VALUES ('#{h}', ...) interpolates admin-entered text into SQL, so a value containing a quote breaks the INSERT with a PG syntax error (or enables injection); fix with ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)

category_id on embeddable_hosts has no foreign key, no index, no default, and no dependent handling (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4-5): deleting a category orphans embeddable_host rows, causing the serializer to emit stale ids, admin UI badge lookup failures, and TopicEmbed.import posting into a nonexistent category; add an FK with on_delete semantics (or nullify), an index, and Category has_many :embeddable_hosts, dependent: :destroy

create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3) silently drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and its data in a shipped production migration; remove the force flag

Half-done case-insensitivity in lookup (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17): where("lower(host) = ?", host) lowercases the column but not the input, and Ruby's URI does not downcase hosts, so a mixed-case referer never matches; fix with host.to_s.downcase

Port-bearing hosts can never match (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 vs :17): the validation regex explicitly permits a :port suffix and before_validation only strips protocol/path, but record_for_host compares the bare uri.host, so an admin saving 'localhost:3000' creates a record that allows nothing; strip the port on save or match host+port

Nil crashes in the hosts controller (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-11, 15-16, 23-24): EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check means an unknown id or missing embeddable_host params raises NoMethodError returning a 500 instead of 404/422; fix with find_by + render_json_error I18n.t('not_found') and params.require(:embeddable_host)

Global store behavior change in the _ids hydration (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:~192-199): the new plural branch unconditionally deletes the *_ids key and calls obj[k].map without checking the value is a non-null array, and _lookupSubType results are not filtered, so missing side-loads produce arrays of undefined; this core-store code affects every payload with a *_ids key, not just embedding; guard the value and only delete/assign when hydration succeeded

Migration create_embeddable_hosts crashes with NoMethodError during db:migrate on any site where the `embed_category` site setting was never explicitly set (the default state, including all fresh installs): the SELECT over site_settings returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises — deploy-blocking on upgrade for nearly every install.

The `if category_id == 0` fallback (lines 13-16) in the migration is dead code — the NoMethodError crash happens before it and a matched row can never yield id 0 — and it shares the same unguarded `[0]['value']` nil-dereference pattern.

Migration inserts old `embeddable_hosts` setting lines verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (which strips scheme and path), so previously-supported entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` can never match `record_for_host`'s bare-hostname comparison — embeds from those hosts silently start returning 403 with no error anywhere.
`val.split("\n")` in the migration inserts empty-string rows for trailing newlines, creating garbage blank rows in the admin table that are never validated.
The migration irreversibly deletes the original `embeddable_hosts` site setting (line 31), so the pre-upgrade host list is not recoverable if the migration goes wrong.

SQL string interpolation in the migration INSERT (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) uses unescaped user-entered data — a single quote anywhere in the old setting crashes the migration mid-run, and it is a textbook injection shape (limited exploitability since data is prior admin input, but not zero).
`create_table ..., force: true` in the migration will silently drop any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table and its data instead of failing loudly.
`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` 500s on a nonexistent id: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil, so `save_host(nil)` hits `nil.host=` and raises NoMethodError.
`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` 500s when the host record is nil — a normal-usage scenario when two admins (or two tabs) delete the same host, the second DELETE returns 500.

`save_host` returns a 500 instead of a 422 validation error on malformed params: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the key is absent, and a nil host value reaches `nil.sub!` in the model's before_validation.

The client's `delete` action in embeddable-host.js.es6 calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE is silently swallowed — the bootbox closes, the row silently stays, and retries keep 500ing until reload.

`Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a silent-pass no-op: it only re-renders the serialized embedding and never persists anything, yet returns 200 — the shipped JS `saveChanges` action would report success while saving nothing (latent since it's unwired in the template, but the endpoint lies about update semantics).

Store hydration plural branch: `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError when a `*_ids` value is null/absent, and since it runs inside the forEach over payload keys, one bad key aborts hydration of the entire payload, not just that association.

Store hydration plural branch: `hydrated || []` is dead code since Array#map is never falsy, so a record missing from the side-load silently becomes an `undefined` element in the hydrated array, rendering as a blank/garbage row downstream with no error.

Store hydration plural branch unconditionally deletes any key matching `_ids` and replaces it (unlike the singular branch which only rewrites when hydration succeeds), so any pre-existing payload key ending in `_ids` that is not a side-loaded association silently loses its value.

Fabricator file contents are swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains the `embeddable_host` fabricator (which depends on category) while all four `category` fabricators moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` — it only works because Fabrication registers by name, not filename, and anyone editing category_fabricator.rb to change category fixtures will instead be editing the host fabricator.

The only controller specs (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb) are vacuous — they only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController` and pass even if create/update/destroy are entirely broken; combined with zero request-level coverage, the migration crash, normalization regression, and nil-500s all shipped under a suite that cannot detect them.

On save, the server defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the client executes `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` with a null categoryId (undefined result), so the UI shows a blank category while the server stored Uncategorized — until reload; this fires on the default add-host flow.

`edit()` seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id`; if the host's category failed to hydrate (e.g., the category was deleted after configuration), `categoryId` is null and an admin who only meant to fix the hostname silently resets the posting category to Uncategorized on save.

")` and each entry is inserted via raw SQL without stripping/rejecting blanks: `records.each do |h| execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)" end`. If the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting contains blank lines (e.g., consecutive `
` or trailing newline), `split("
")` will include `""` entries, which will be inserted as empty-string `host` rows (allowed by `null: false`). These would then appear in `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` via `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` and render as junk/blank rows in the admin table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost's format regex explicitly allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}) and before_validation only strips scheme and path, so an admin can save hosts like localhost:3000 or example.com:8080, but record_for_host compares only uri.host (which never includes a port), so port-bearing records silently never authorize any request — either strip ports on save or match against host+port.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` callback strips only scheme and path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), leaving any port intact (e.g. `example.com:8080`). However, `record_for_host` parses a URL via `URI(host)` and compares only `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no referential integrity between embeddable_hosts.category_id and categories (no model validation, no DB foreign key, and category deletion does not clean up hosts): orphaned hosts cause TopicEmbed.import to pass a dead category_id to PostCreator (category: eh.try(:category_id)), breaking subsequent embeds/feed polls, and in the admin UI host.category hydrates to nothing so the edit dialog shows an empty category chooser and saving silently reassigns the host to uncategorized without warning.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds PUT /admin/customize/embedding (routes.rb) implemented by Admin::EmbeddingController#update, but that action does not read any params or persist anything; it only re-renders the current @embedding (embedding_controller.rb). On the frontend, admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 defines a saveChanges action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that no-op endpoint if invoked. Even if the current template (admin/templates/embedding.hbs) doesn’t wire up `saveChanges`, the API surface is misleading: it advertises an update capability that isn’t implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unquoted string interpolation in the migration INSERT: old setting values are spliced into raw SQL via VALUES ('#{h}', ...), so a value containing a quote aborts/corrupts the migration (an unparameterized SQL vector), and split("\n") can yield blank lines that insert '' hosts which can never match

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, where `h` comes from splitting the old `site_settings.value` (`val.split("\n")`). This is unescaped/unparameterized: a host value containing a single quote will break the SQL (or worse), and blank lines from the split are not filtered/stripped, so `''` can be inserted into `embeddable_hosts.host` (allowed by the DB schema), bypassing model validation and leaving invalid data behind.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dotless hostnames like localhost are no longer savable: the regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` so dotless intranet names are rejected, whereas the old setting compared raw strings and matched them — a capability regression for environments that legitimately embed from localhost/dotless intranet hosts, with only the dev-mode admin bypass remaining

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host` with a regex requiring a dot + TLD segment (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), which will reject dotless hosts like `localhost` or intranet names (e.g. `intranet`). Previously, `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` could allow such entries because it ultimately compared raw strings (falling back to `h` when `URI(h).host` was nil) against `URI(embed_url).host`, so `localhost` could match. Now embedding authorization uses `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which would work for `http://localhost` if a record existed, but the validation prevents creating/saving that record—making this a verifiable capability regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch destroys raw *_ids keys even when hydration fails: it unconditionally delete obj[k] and replaces it with pluralize(subType) even when _lookupSubType returns undefined for some ids, producing [undefined, ...] since `hydrated || []` never fires on a truthy array, and obj[k].map throws TypeError if a serializer emits *_ids: null; previously plural *_ids keys passed through untouched

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was extended to match `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the plural branch it does `obj[k].map(...)` without guarding for `null`/non-array values, which would throw if a serializer emits `*_ids: null`. It also unconditionally `delete obj[k]` and assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`, but `hydrated` is always a truthy array, so missing lookups can yield `[undefined, ...]` and the raw `*_ids` key is removed even when hydration fails—unlike the singular branch which only deletes when hydration succeeds. Previously `*_ids` keys would not be touched at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts crashes with NoMethodError on default data: when no valid 'embed_category' site_settings row exists (fresh installs, sites that never set it, or values matching a renamed/deleted category since the join matches on c.name = s.value), the SELECT returns zero rows and result[0]['id'] raises on nil, aborting db:migrate and blocking deploys; the fallback at lines 14-16 is unreachable because it is gated on category_id == 0 (ids start at 1) and uncategorized_category_id is a computed SiteSetting helper method, not a row in site_settings

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` to derive `category_id` from a join on `site_settings` (name='embed_category') and `categories` (c.name = s.value). If that SELECT returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. This is directly verifiable from the diff; the later fallback only runs after this access and therefore cannot prevent the crash when there are no rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies old embeddable_hosts setting values into the table verbatim without normalization, but the new authorization check (where('lower(host) = ?', uri.host)) only matches a bare lowercase hostname; old values with http(s):// prefixes or paths (explicitly supported by the removed code) never match since before_validation normalization only runs on save, never on the migration's raw INSERTs, so existing embeds silently start failing EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? with 403s and no error surfaced anywhere

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without going through the `EmbeddableHost` model, so its `before_validation` normalization (stripping `http(s)://` and paths) never runs. The new authorization path `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the request URL and then matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, which only matches bare hostnames. Any migrated rows containing `http://...` or `/path` (explicitly supported by the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` code) will not match and will cause `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false, leading to `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raising `InvalidAccess` (403).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration's INSERT interpolates the host value h unescaped into SQL, so a stored setting line containing a quote character aborts the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops over each line `h` from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting and executes raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is not escaped/quoted via the DB adapter, any host line containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) can break the SQL and abort the migration (and also presents SQL injection risk from stored data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy pass EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first straight into save_host/host.destroy with no nil check, so a stale id (record deleted in another session, double-click/double-delete) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404 or render_json_error, leaving the frontend promise unresolved

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code fetches with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`). If the record is missing (stale/double-delete/etc.), `host` will be `nil`, causing `save_host` to call `host.host = ...` or `destroy` to call `nil.destroy`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 instead of a handled 404/error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost category_id is never validated and is not cleaned up on category deletion: save_host only coerces blank category_ids to uncategorized while any non-blank numeric value is stored (Rails 4 belongs_to adds no presence validation), and nothing wires EmbeddableHost into Category#destroy, so deleted categories orphan rows and TopicEmbed.import passes the dead category_id to PostCreator with skip_validations: true, causing silent import failures or topics referencing a nonexistent category, with the admin UI showing a blank badge and no error

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost` only validates `host` format and has `belongs_to :category` with no presence/existence validation (Rails 4 does not auto-validate). `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` and only coerces *blank* to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, so any non-blank (including nonexistent) id can be persisted. There is also no `dependent:` behavior or other linkage shown to clean up `embeddable_hosts` when a `Category` is destroyed, so orphaned `category_id`s are possible. Downstream, `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` when creating posts, and the admin UI renders `category-badge host.category`, which would be nil for an orphaned id. This is a real correctness/data-integrity issue exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed requests produce 500s instead of 4xx in the embeddable hosts admin flow: params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises when the embeddable_host key is absent, and a JSON null host makes before_validation's self.host.sub! raise NoMethodError on nil before the format validation can return a friendly 422

Frontend destroyRecord().then(...) in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch (the sibling save correctly uses .catch(popupAjaxError)), so a failed DELETE silently leaves the row in place with no user feedback and an unhandled promise rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` without any `.catch(...)` handler. By contrast, `save()` explicitly does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE request fails, there will be no user feedback and the rejected promise is unhandled; the row is only removed inside the `.then`, so it will remain with no error surfaced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op: the update action ignores the request body entirely and re-renders the same payload as show, while the frontend saveChanges PUTs {} with no error handling — a success-without-persist trap for any future embedding settings added to this singleton

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) without reading params or persisting anything, so `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` is effectively a no-op (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). The frontend controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` and does not attach error handling (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`). However, the current UI/template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) doesn’t invoke `saveChanges` and the only persisted changes (hosts) go through `EmbeddableHostsController`, so this is more of a misleading/incomplete endpoint that could become a trap if settings are later added, rather than a presently broken behavior proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new plural *_ids hydration branch in store.js.es6 is unguarded and changes key-deletion behavior globally: obj[k].map has no presence check (category_ids: null throws a TypeError that kills hydration for the whole model), it unconditionally deletes the *_ids key even when _lookupSubType hydrates nothing (unlike the singular branch, an un-side-loaded *_ids payload loses its ids and gains an array of undefined), and it writes to naive pluralize(subType) (category_ids -> obj.categorys)

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6, the new plural hydration branch `if (m[2]) { const hydrated = obj[k].map(...); obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k]; }` is unguarded: if `obj[k]` is `null`/`undefined` (e.g. `category_ids: null`), calling `.map` will throw a TypeError and break hydration. It also unconditionally deletes the original `*_ids` key and replaces it with an array of whatever `_lookupSubType` returns (potentially `undefined` entries) even when the side-loaded data isn't present, unlike the singular branch which only deletes when hydration succeeds. The specific claim about `pluralize(subType)` producing bad plurals (e.g. `categorys`) can’t be verified from this diff because `pluralize` implementation isn’t shown, but the presence-check and unconditional deletion issues are directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After save, embeddable-host.js.es6 overwrites host.category from the local categoryId instead of the server response: when no category was chosen the server defaults to uncategorized but Discourse.Category.findById(null/undefined) returns nothing, so the badge renders blank and the row disagrees with persisted state until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, after `host.save(props)` resolves, the client unconditionally overwrites the model with `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`; if `categoryId` is null/undefined (e.g., for a new host where no category was chosen), `findById` returns nothing and the UI will show a blank badge even though the persisted `category_id` is uncategorized until reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no uniqueness validation or unique index on embeddable_host.host and where('lower(host) = ?', host).first has no ORDER BY, so entering the same host twice with different categories makes record_for_host's pick — and therefore which category imported topics land in — arbitrary and nondeterministic between queries

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds EmbeddableHost without any uniqueness validation on `host` (only `validates_format_of`) and the migration `create_embeddable_hosts` creates no unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host`. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no `ORDER BY`, so if duplicate rows exist for the same host (e.g., different `category_id`), which row is returned is not guaranteed. Since `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` to choose the category, imported topic categorization becomes nondeterministic when duplicates are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The host format validation regex requires a dotted TLD of 2-5 characters, rejecting dot-less hostnames (localhost, internal names) and longer TLDs that the old free-form setting allowed, breaking intranet/self-hosted embedding setups (dev is only saved by the Rails.env.development? && admin? bypass in embed_controller)

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`, which requires a dot and a 2–5 character TLD. Combined with the `before_validation` normalization that strips scheme and paths, this will reject valid previously-allowed host entries like `localhost`, internal dot-less names, and longer modern TLDs (>5). Since the old `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` (type `host_list`) is removed and host checks now rely on `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, this is a behavior-breaking regression for intranet/self-hosted embedding setups; the dev/admin bypass in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only avoids it in that specific development case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data migration create_embeddable_hosts (20150818190757) crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row doesn't exist — the default state for most installs since Discourse persists only overridden settings — aborting db:migrate on upgrade; it crashes the same way when the stored value doesn't match a category name, and the 'if category_id == 0' fallback to uncategorized_category_id is unreachable dead code

Migration inserts legacy host values via raw SQL INSERT without the model's before_validation normalization (protocol/path stripping), so entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim and never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's exact 'lower(host) = ?' lookup, silently breaking embedding from previously-allowed hosts after upgrade while the Fabricate-based specs pass

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` copies legacy `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` lines into the new `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, so values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are persisted verbatim. The model normalization that strips protocol/path is in `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation`, but it is bypassed by the migration. Later allow-checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the URL and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, e.g. `discourse.org`, which will not match a stored `http://discourse.org` row. This can break previously-allowed hosts after upgrade, while Fabricate-based specs (which create records through the model and thus normalize) would not catch it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped string interpolation of host values into the migration's SQL INSERT — a host containing a quote kills the migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` interpolates host strings directly into raw SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), it will break the SQL and can cause the migration to fail (and is also an injection risk). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Both new admin controllers (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController) have placeholder-only specs asserting superclass inheritance; no request specs cover create/update/destroy happy paths, the render_json_error branch on invalid hosts, the blank-category_id defaulting to uncategorized, or the serialization shape, giving a false impression the controllers are tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new admin controllers with real behavior (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy plus save_host defaulting blank category_id to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returning render_json_error on validation failure; Admin::EmbeddingController#show/#update rendering EmbeddingSerializer). However, the only new controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) merely assert the superclass inheritance and do not exercise any controller actions, response codes/bodies, error branches, defaulting behavior, or serialization shape—so they can misleadingly suggest coverage where there is none.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy on a nonexistent id and requests with missing params[:embeddable_host] raise uncaught NoMethodError and return 500 instead of 404, and no spec exercises these unknown-id or malformed-param paths

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` but do not handle `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` and `save_host` immediately dereferences (`host.host = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`; both will raise `NoMethodError` and yield a 500 for nonexistent IDs. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present and does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which will also raise `NoMethodError` on malformed/missing params. The added controller specs only assert subclassing and do not cover these error paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero frontend tests for the entire new admin embedding UI, including the pathFor override, the ADMIN_MODELS basePath change shared by all admin models, addHost/deleteHost, the buffered save/cancel/delete flows, the post-save client-side category patch, and the store hydration the page depends on (plural *_ids hydration tested only via the single-word 'color' fixture, not the real multi-word 'embeddable_host_ids' consumer)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a brand-new admin embedding UI surface (adapter `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` with `pathFor`, route/controller/templates, and `embeddable-host` component with buffered edit/save/cancel/delete flows and client-side `category` patch after save), plus shared infrastructure changes (`RestAdapter` `ADMIN_MODELS`/`basePath` behavior and `store._hydrateEmbedded` supporting `*_ids`). In the diff, there are no new frontend tests covering the new admin embedding route/controller/component behavior or the admin adapter/basePath interaction; the only JS tests touched are `store-test.js.es6` and pretender fixtures, which test plural `*_ids` hydration only via the simple `color_ids` case, not the actual multi-word `embeddable_host_ids` consumer implied by `EmbeddingSerializer` (`has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale vacuous topic_spec test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' survives the behavioral change where expandable_first_post? no longer consults embeddable hosts; it passes only for unrelated reasons (embed_truncate defaults false, has_topic_embed? false on unstubbed Fabricate.build), and the actual change (embed + truncate + zero hosts now returns true) has no test documenting it

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb), so embeddable hosts are no longer consulted. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` now asserts `false` without setting `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` or stubbing `has_topic_embed?`, so it passes due to defaults/unstubbed behavior rather than verifying anything about hosts. This makes the test stale/vacuous and the new behavior (truth depending only on truncate + embed, even with no hosts configured) is not explicitly documented by a targeted spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weakened embed_controller_spec 'missing host' test passes for the wrong reason: it fabricates no host but also doesn't stub a referer, so it fails via the nil-referer path instead of the no-hosts path and can't distinguish the two conditions

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the "raises an error with a missing host" test no longer sets up a "no hosts configured" condition (it removed `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`) and also does not stub `request.referer`. With the code change in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (now only `raise ... unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`), the request will fail because `request.referer` is nil/invalid (since `URI(nil)` is rescued to nil in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`), not specifically because there are no allowed host records. This makes the test pass for a less specific reason and it cannot distinguish "no allowed hosts" from "missing/invalid referer" after the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that accepts nothing and changes nothing (just re-serializes), and embedding.hbs renders no control that sends the frontend saveChanges action, making the PUT dead code — saving embedding settings silently does nothing and nothing in the suite would reveal it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without persisting anything (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`), and the Ember controller defines a `saveChanges` action calling `embedding.update({})` (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`). However, `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` provides no button/control wired to `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and per-host save/delete via `EmbeddableHostsController`). This makes the PUT route/action effectively dead code in this PR, but it doesn't demonstrably break host CRUD (which uses `/admin/embeddable_hosts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in TopicEmbed.import fallback category is untested: category assignment changed from the global SiteSetting.embed_category to eh.try(:category_id) derived from the URL's host, so when the host isn't a registered EmbeddableHost (e.g., RSS feed polling) topics now silently post to Uncategorized instead of the previously configured category; the spec only covers the matched-host path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes TopicEmbed.import to set PostCreator's category from an EmbeddableHost match (`eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then `category: eh.try(:category_id)`), replacing the previous global `SiteSetting.embed_category` (and that setting is removed from site_settings.yml/server locale). In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the new test setup always Fabricates(:embeddable_host) and asserts the matched-host category path, but there is no test for the non-matching-host case where `eh` is nil and `category` becomes nil (which likely falls back to a default/Uncategorized behavior). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing edge-case test for a behavioral change, but the diff doesn’t prove it’s an actual defect vs intended per-host categorization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New plural hydration branch in store.js (lines 192-197) lacks the singular branch's guardrails: obj[k].map has no null/undefined guard (a null *_ids in any payload throws), failed lookups aren't filtered, and 'hydrated || []' is dead code since arrays are always truthy — failed lookups produce [undefined] records; only the happy path is tested

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch matches keys ending in `*_ids` and unconditionally calls `obj[k].map(...)` (lines around 192-197). If a payload includes an `*_ids` key with a `null`/`undefined` value, this will throw at runtime. Unlike the singular `*_id` branch, it also does not guard against failed lookups (it will produce `[undefined, ...]`), and `hydrated || []` is ineffective because `map` always returns a truthy array. The added JS tests only cover the happy path where `color_ids` is an array, not these edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents appear accidentally swapped: the :embeddable_host fabricator is defined in category_fabricator.rb and all four category fabricators are in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — functionally harmless but a botched rename that will misdirect anyone maintaining these fixtures

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb raises NoMethodError on default and fresh installs: when the embed_category setting is unset (its default is an empty string and no category can be named empty), the INNER JOIN matches nothing so [0] is nil and [0]['id'].to_i raises; the `if category_id == 0` fallback never executes and contains the same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern for uncategorized_category_id, so db:migrate aborts for every site that never set embed_category and for all fresh installs

If the query returns zero rows (e.g., embed_category unset/empty so the JOIN matches nothing), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration's raw-SQL INSERT stores host values unnormalized, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation protocol/path stripping, while record_for_host matches via lower(host) = uri.host: previously tolerated 'http://'-prefixed entries become rows like 'http://discourse.org' that can never match, so previously working embeds are silently rejected after upgrade, and the DB is left holding rows the model's own format validation would reject

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies each line from the old `site_settings` value directly into the table via raw SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` 500s on a nonexistent id: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil, so `save_host(nil)` hits `nil.host=` and raises NoMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), so if the id is nonexistent and `host` is `nil`, it will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` 500s when the host record is nil — a normal-usage scenario when two admins (or two tabs) delete the same host, the second DELETE returns 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally `host.destroy` is called. If the record doesn’t exist (e.g., already deleted in another tab/admin), `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise a `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `save_host` returns a 500 instead of a 422 validation error on malformed params: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the key is absent, and a nil host value reaches `nil.sub!` in the model's before_validation.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code blindly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`), which will raise if `:embeddable_host` is missing or not a hash. Additionally, `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` without a nil guard (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`), so a nil `host` value would raise `NoMethodError` before validation errors can be returned. Both cases would produce a 500 instead of a 422-style validation response on malformed/absent params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client's `delete` action in embeddable-host.js.es6 calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE is silently swallowed — the bootbox closes, the row silently stays, and retries keep 500ing until reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` without any `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE fails, there is no error handling/UI feedback and the row will not be removed because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then` branch, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a silent-pass no-op: it only re-renders the serialized embedding and never persists anything, yet returns 200 — the shipped JS `saveChanges` action would report success while saving nothing (latent since it's unwired in the template, but the endpoint lies about update semantics).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without applying any params or persisting anything; `@embedding` itself is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all`. On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6#saveChanges` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit the new `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` route via the new adapter and receive 200 with the same serialized payload. However, the template `embedding.hbs` doesn’t wire `saveChanges`, and host changes are persisted through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save` / `destroyRecord`). So it’s a real, diff-grounded semantics/architecture issue (a no-op PUT endpoint + unused action), but not a currently verifiable broken behavior in the shipped UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store hydration plural branch: `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError when a `*_ids` value is null/absent, and since it runs inside the forEach over payload keys, one bad key aborts hydration of the entire payload, not just that association.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`if (m[2])`) does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is an array. If a payload includes a `*_ids` key with a `null` value (or other non-array), this will throw a `TypeError` and abort hydration for that object because it runs inside the `Object.keys(obj).forEach` loop. The diff adds no guard (e.g. `Array.isArray(obj[k]) ? ... : []`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store hydration plural branch: `hydrated || []` is dead code since Array#map is never falsy, so a record missing from the side-load silently becomes an `undefined` element in the hydrated array, rendering as a blank/garbage row downstream with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` the new plural branch hydrates `*_ids` via `obj[k].map(...)` and assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), so `|| []` is dead. More importantly, if `_lookupSubType` can’t find a sideloaded record for an id, the mapped array will contain `undefined` entries, and the code still deletes the original `*_ids` key. That can lead to downstream consumers iterating a relationship array that contains `undefined` “records” (blank/garbage rows) with no error and with the ids lost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store hydration plural branch unconditionally deletes any key matching `_ids` and replaces it (unlike the singular branch which only rewrites when hydration succeeds), so any pre-existing payload key ending in `_ids` that is not a side-loaded association silently loses its value.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the plural branch (`if (m[2])`), it always does `delete obj[k];` after mapping IDs, and always sets `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Unlike the singular branch, it does not conditionally rewrite/delete only when hydration succeeds. So any payload field ending with `_ids` (even if not a sideloaded association or if lookup fails) will be removed and replaced with an array of potentially `undefined` entries, silently losing the original value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On save, the server defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the client executes `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` with a null categoryId (undefined result), so the UI shows a blank category while the server stored Uncategorized — until reload; this fires on the default add-host flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host` component `save()`, the client always sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and after save does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` (component `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`). On the default add-host flow, `categoryId` starts as `null` and can remain unset if the admin doesn’t choose a category (`categoryId: null` + template `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}`). Server-side `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. With a null `categoryId`, `findById(null)` yields `undefined`, so `host.category` becomes blank in the UI even though the server saved Uncategorized, until reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `edit()` seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id`; if the host's category failed to hydrate (e.g., the category was deleted after configuration), `categoryId` is null and an admin who only meant to fix the hostname silently resets the posting category to Uncategorized on save.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `edit()` sets `categoryId` from `this.get('host.category.id')`. If `host.category` is missing (e.g., category deleted or not hydrated), `categoryId` becomes null/undefined. Then `save()` always does `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`, and the server-side `save_host` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` coerces a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. So an admin editing only the hostname can unintentionally reset the posting category to Uncategorized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The model's validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and before_validation doesn't strip it, but `record_for_host` matches `lower(host) = uri.host` where `URI#host` never includes a port — so an admin can save `example.com:3000` and it silently authorizes nothing, a dead whitelist entry with zero feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, the validation regex permits an optional port segment `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and path but not the port (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` then `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). As a result, saving `http://example.com:3000` will persist `example.com:3000`. However `record_for_host` parses the referer/embed URL with `URI(...)` and matches using `uri.host` (host only, no port) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Since `URI#host` excludes the port, a stored value like `example.com:3000` will never match a referer `http://example.com:3000/...` (which yields `uri.host == "example.com"`), creating a silently non-functional whitelist entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The validation regex's `{2,5}` TLD cap rejects legitimate long gTLDs such as `.photography`.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added model `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the validation `validates_format_of :host, :with => /...\.[a-z]{2,5}.../i` explicitly caps the TLD length to 5 characters. This will reject valid modern gTLDs longer than 5 (e.g. `.photography`), preventing legitimate embeddable hosts from being saved/used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no uniqueness constraint (migration or validation) on embeddable hosts, so duplicate and case-variant hosts can be stored with arbitrary first-match-wins behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The new `embeddable_hosts` table migration (`create_embeddable_hosts`) adds `host` without any unique index, and the model `EmbeddableHost` has only a format validation (no `validates_uniqueness_of`). As a result, duplicate hosts (including case variants, since `before_validation` strips scheme/path but does not normalize case) can be stored. Lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `record_for_host`, so duplicates lead to arbitrary “first” selection; this affects behavior such as choosing the category in `TopicEmbed.import` (`eh.try(:category_id)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Auth asymmetry: the embedding/embeddable_hosts routes demand admin via `AdminConstraint.new`, but the controllers' before_filter chain stops at `ensure_staff` (moderators included) — enforcement lives only in the routing layer, so any future route exposure or reuse of these actions outside the constrained scope would silently grant moderators control over embed whitelisting (hardening concern, not a live vulnerability).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a mismatch: routes for `customize/embedding` and `resources :embeddable_hosts` are protected by `constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only at routing), but the new controllers only add `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` (and `:fetch_embedding`) (moderators are staff). If these actions were ever exposed via another route (or the constraint changed/removed), the controller-level guard would allow non-admin staff to manage embeddable hosts. This is a hardening/consistency concern; whether it’s a live vulnerability depends on what `Admin::AdminController` already enforces, which isn’t shown in the diff.
